A stable implementation is a masked, normalized recurrence (an implementation derivation): initialize numerator n[B,D]=0 and mass z[B,1]=0 in float32. For each position t, let m=(sequence[:,t]!=0)[:,None], e=item_emb(sequence[:,t]).float(); compute n=torch.where(m, decay*n+e, n), z=torch.where(m, decay*z+1, z), and h_t=n/z.clamp_min(1e-8), with 0≤decay≤1. Stack outputs without detaching to preserve gradients. This avoids inverse exponential powers and their overflow. Left padding contributes nothing; reset state for each supplied truncated history. h_t includes the current observed item, appropriate when predicting the next item; mask padded training positions.

Carry both paths explicitly: log2feats(sequence) returns torch.cat([context, history],dim=-1), shape B×L×2D, where context is the causally masked SASRec representation and history contains h_t. predict_score splits features into c,h and computes contextual and transition dot products, optionally using separate candidate embeddings: for items B×L×2, score=(c.unsqueeze(-2)*E_context(items)).sum(-1)+alpha*(h.unsqueeze(-2)*E_transition(items)).sum(-1), yielding B×L×2. Final-position inference uses features[:,-1,:] with B×K candidates through the same scoring function. Adapt diagnostic dimension assumptions and retain the required probe interfaces.

Verify with model.eval() and torch.no_grad(): compare batched scores[:,-1,:] against final-feature scoring on identical candidates; test left padding, empty/singleton histories, and truncation. Compare prefix results only with identical retained history and positional indices. Repeat after constructing the identical architecture and strict checkpoint reload; save architecture configuration, decay, and mixing parameters, and update the predictor writer. PyTorch documents that eval() controls dropout and state_dict contains parameters and persistent buffers ([Module documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html)). These are proposed checks, not measured results.
